issue_context.title: RepresenterError with looped lookups in YAML callback
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
Loading template files in a loop leads to RepresenterErrors using YAML callback

Note that in the real world, this can manifest itself in the task erroring out, although I can't reproduce that in a more minimal test case as yet - I hope that the below information is enough to eliminate the underlying issue.

Other notes: 
* If I remove the trailing `-`, the task succeeds. But I added the trailing dash to counter #49579
* This works fine if I use the default stdout callback
* If there is only one element in the loop, we don't see the problem(!)

- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME

        {{ kube_resource_manifests_from_files + lookup('template', item)| from_yaml_all | list }}

It looks like this started happening with the UnsafeProxy removal in 164881d871964aa64e0f911d03ae270acbad253c. cc @mkrizek

I am focused somewhere else currently but from a quick glance we seem to be missing a representer for `AnsibleUnsafeBytes`, similar to what we have for `AnsibleUnsafeText` in https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/95525030e2d2bcf2bb1a145700ecdf80f6a7567b/lib/ansible/parsing/yaml/dumper.py#L57-L60

review_comments:
Little more accurate version of this comment
```
            # https://pyyaml.org/wiki/PyYAMLDocumentation#string-conversion-python-2-only
            # pyyaml on Python 2 can return either unicode or bytes when given byte strings.
            # We normalize that to always return unicode on Python2 as that's right most of the
            # time.  However, this means byte strings can round trip through yaml on Python3 but
            # not on Python2.  To make this code work the same on Python2 and Python3 (we want
            # the Python3 behaviour) we need to change the methods in Ansible to:
            # (1) Let byte strings pass through yaml without being converted on Python2
            # (2) Convert byte strings to text strings before being given to pyyaml  (Without this,
            #       strings would end up as byte strings most of the time which would mostly be wrong)
            # In practice, we mostly read bytes in from files and then pass that to pyyaml, for which
            # the present behavior is correct.
            # This is a workaround for the current behavior.
```
